details:
- CVE-2026-33818: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to enforce a
  maximum recursion depth in encoding/asn1 Unmarshal, preventing stack exhaustion when
  parsing deeply-nested recursive structures
- CVE-2026-39820: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to fix quadratic
  complexity in consumeComment in net/mail, preventing CPU exhaustion and excessive memory
  allocation from well-crafted input to ParseAddress, ParseAddressList and ParseDate
- CVE-2026-42499: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to fix quadratic
  consumePhrase behaviour in net/mail, preventing denial-of-service when parsing an email
  address according to RFC 5322
- CVE-2026-56858: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to fix JavaScript
  regexp context tracking in html/template so pathological input can no longer close an
  unescaped '/' early and inject attacker-controlled content
- CVE-2026-56859: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to add a recursion
  depth guard during decode in encoding/xml so DecodeElement no longer resets the depth
  counter, preventing stack exhaustion
- CVE-2026-56860: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to avoid quadratic
  complexity in net/url resolvePath by resolving '..' segments with index-based backtracking
  on a byte buffer
- CVE-2026-56862: rebuild against golang >= 1.25.7-1.el9_6.tuxcare.els16 to stop counting
  handshake messages as state-advancing after the handshake has completed in crypto/tls,
  bounding the key derivation work a client can force with repeated KeyUpdate messages
